claims.summary: (a) Deterministically, every grid function g on a mesh delta with 1/delta an integer and discrete cost sum_e delta^2 psi_4^*(|Delta_e g|/(2 delta)) at most M has TV(g) <= T(M) = 4 + 2M/psi_4^*(1), psi_4^*(1) = 0.461650. (c) Deterministically, for meshes delta_0 <= W with W/delta_0 and 1/W integers and any cost sum_e delta_0^2 psi^*(v_e/2) with psi^* convex, nondecreasing and zero at zero (one per direction), the averages E_W g cost on the mesh W at most what g costs. (b) For N large, on the event of lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a) at kappa = 4, for every dyadic delta_0 in [4 sqrt(log N/N), W], W = 2^(-l_1), and every g on it of cost at most M at (4,4): |D(g) - D(E_W g)| <= c_4 T(M) sqrt(N log N).
claims.assessment: Working proof, passed with corrections in two passes of one medium reviewer (research/results/ultimate_matching_one_height_rounding_20261017/review.txt):(a) edges with v < 2 give at most 4, the others delta^2 v <= 2 w_e/psi^*(1) since psi^*(t)/t is nondecreasing; (b) lem:cut-cell-variance-bound (a), (W/delta_0)^2 < sqrt(log N)/4; (c) a coarse increment over W is an average of r^3 fine increments over delta_0 inside the pair of coarse cells, Jensen, and each fine edge's weights over the pairs containing it sum to at most one.
claims.rationale: Moves every grid function of the class from any dyadic mesh in range to the single Leighton-Shor mesh at an O(sqrt(N log N)) cost, at no increase of cost.

claims.summary: On the event that every cell of every dyadic mesh delta >= 4 sqrt(log N/N) has |n_Q - N delta^2| <= C_0 sqrt(N delta^2 log N), C_0 = 15/4, at (4,4), for every such delta, every M > 0, every Y >= 2e^16 and every grid function h on mesh delta with discrete cost at most M, some theta in [0,1) makes r = Y delta(floor(h/(Y delta) + theta) - theta) satisfy 0 <= h - r < Y delta, r - min r a nested chain at the one height Y, cost(r) <= 7M + (psi_4^*(Y/2)/Y) T(M), and |D(h) - D(r)| <= C_0 Y sqrt(N log N).
claims.assessment: Working proof, passed with corrections in two passes of one medium reviewer (research/results/ultimate_matching_one_height_rounding_20261017/review.txt):the error by per-cell counts; edges with v >= Y at most double their increment (doubling of psi_4^* at t >= e^16), edges with v < Y cross a level with probability v/Y over a uniform theta, at expected cost (psi^*(Y/2)/Y) TV.
claims.rationale: Presents every class function at a given mesh as a one-height chain up to O(sqrt(N log N)), so that the record's chain lemmas apply to the steep part of any class function; functions with close values alone were already bounded by lem:cost-weighted-slope-bound (a).

claims.summary: At (4,4), with Y = e^22, C1 = 14 + (psi_4^*(Y/2)/Y) T(2) <= 30.18, c = C1/2 and y* = Y/c >= e^19.28 >= 2e^16: if with probability tending to one every nested chain W y* sum_k 1_{A_k} at the one height y* on the mesh W = 2^(-l_1) with discrete cost at most 2 at (4,4) has |D| <= C_2 sqrt(N log N), then with probability tending to one every grid function on a dyadic mesh delta_0 in [4 sqrt(log N/N), W] with discrete cost at most 2 at (4,4) has |D(g)| <= (c_4 T(2) + C_0 Y + c C_2) sqrt(N log N); conversely; since every grid function on the mesh W rounds to such a chain, one height is no restriction there, and the net content is the reduction of the dyadic proxy from every finer mesh to the mesh W.
claims.assessment: Working proof, passed with corrections in two passes of one medium reviewer (research/results/ultimate_matching_one_height_rounding_20261017/review.txt):lem:leighton-shor-mesh-averaging at M = 2 (averages of cost at most 2), then lem:one-height-rounding at the mesh W with M = 2, then scaling by 1/c.
